reason: The cited evidence shows fluorine treatment improves oxidation resistance in TiAl alloys via Al₂O₃ formation (E3, E4), but none of the cited passages address HfNbTaTiZr, refractory oxide formation, or the preservation of mechanical properties in this alloy system. The key premise that the mechanism transfers to a chemically distinct HEA is unsupported, and E1 only notes that coatings are needed without providing evidence for the proposed treatment.
premises: Fluorine surface treatment promotes formation of a protective Al₂O₃ film on TiAl alloys at 1000 °C
A dense, adherent oxide film can reduce oxygen uptake during high-temperature air exposure
The treatment does not degrade the bulk mechanical properties of the substrate alloy
Refractory oxides (HfO₂, Ta₂O₅) will form a continuous protective layer on HfNbTaTiZr under similar conditions
The fluorine effect observed in TiAl alloys is transferable to refractory high-entropy alloys
